I see a potential bug in `add_minimal_typeobj` for the STRUCTURE case. Look at this error handling:

```c
if ((ret = ddsi_type_register_dep (gv, &xt->id, &xt->_u.structure.members.seq[n].type, &mto->_u.struct_type.member_seq._buffer[n].common.member_type_id)) != DDS_RETCODE_OK)
{
  for (uint32_t m = 0; m < n - 1; m++)
    ddsi_type_unref_locked (gv, xt->_u.structure.members.seq[m].type);
  ...
}
```

The loop `for (uint32_t m = 0; m < n - 1; m++)` should be `m < n` (or `m <= n-1`). When `n=0`, `n-1` underflows to a huge number (UINT32_MAX), so the loop iterates over uninitialized memory. But more importantly, when `n > 0`, the loop only unrefs members `0` to `n-2`, missing member `n-1`. This means member `n-1`'s type is not unref'd, but then `ddsrt_free(xt->_u.structure.members.seq)` is called, and later `ddsi_xt_type_fini` will try to unref the member types again (including the already-freed ones) - causing a use-after-free.
